title: Aime Barelli returns defeated and receives Briggs's trumpet
summary: The Nice trumpeter Aime Barelli, back from the army with only his mouthpiece, was taken in by Briggs, given a civilian outfit and his trumpet, and introduced to Charles Delaunay.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Right.
Aime Barelli came back to Paris. He was from Nice.
Barelli, you should explain.

He came back as a beaten soldier, more or less. He had nothing and he had no where to go. He didn't know anybody in Paris, but he went to the local, and asked where he could find me. They gave him an address and he came up to see me.
I should just interrupt and say, that Barelli was one of
Briggs 343
the finest of the French jazz musicians.
Oh, yes, one of the finest. He spent thirty years at "The Sportin'" in Monte Carlo, and he was just reinstated about six months ago.
He had finished and he was reinstated about six months ago.

And Aime and I were great, great friends, when I first met him in 1935, and I was at the casino in Cannes, and he used to come over with his group after they finished at their casino in Nice, and sit in the cabaret, and listen to the orchestra.
Well, he was such a fine boy, he came to see me. And his first words were, "Arthur, I'm here."

I said, "I'm glad you're here". (Laughter). I said, "I'm glad you're here, glad to see you Aimé." And he said, "Yes, but I know no one, and I have no place to go." I said, "You don't have to worry," I said, "But have you got your mouthpiece?"
Briggs 344
He said, "Yes, I have it, it's the only thing that I have." He took it out. He said, "It's the only thing I saved." He was in a beaten up uniform, so I gave him a civilian outfit and everything.
And he said, "But I have to live." So I said, "Well, look, for the time being you just camp -- the best way, you camp here with me, until I see Charles Delaunay, and you'll certainly find work."

He said, "But I got no instrument." I said, "Yes, you have." "That's mine, now that's yours." So I gave it to him. I said, "I'm through with it for the time being. I'm through and you'd honor my horn," I said. I said, "I know, 'cause I've heard you play, and you'll honor my horn." I said, "It's yours."
So he took my horn and the following day we went down to Hot Club of France together, and fortunately Charles Delaunay was there.
The Hot Club is in
Briggs
Rue Chaptal 14e.
Rue Chaptal 14e.
14 Rue Chaptal 14e.
That same building
Yes, the same place, yes.
You were living where, at that time?
Not far from here, Rue Felixiene, number 7. Say about 500 yards from this apartment.
Right.

And I'd taken him down to where, Charles Delaunay was there, and other members, and they said, 'Well, we'll do all we can for him.' They found him work and everything else. And he came up to my house whenever he wanted to, and we got along nicely.
